MA Mannan with Nur Hossain Chowdhury, Advocates—For the Petitioners.

Monir Miah & others ------ Petitioners

Shafiqur Rahman and others ------ Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
The petitioners as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 41 of 1998 in the 3rd Court of Joint District Judge, Sylhet for preemption of the suit land under the Mohammedan Law stating, inter alia, that the suit property was a dwelling property in nature. Abdur Razzak, the predecessor of the plaintiffs and defendants Nos. 9-11, Abdul Hakim, Hajee Abdul Bari, the predecessors of defendants Nos. 2-8, Ramjan Bibi, Abdul Gani, the predecessors of defendants Nos. 12-19 and defendant No. 20 were the owners of the suit property and SA Khatians Nos. 9, 46, 98, 160, 200 and 267 were correctly prepared in their names. The plaintiffs were the successors of Abdur Razzak and Dhan Miah and they had been possessing the other land jointly with the other co-sharers. On 9-2-1405 BS, at about 7-30 AM defendant No. 21 along with a labourer was putting fence on the suit property. On query made by plaintiff No. 1, defendant No. 21 informed him that his brother, defendant No. 1 purchased the suit property from defendants Nos. 2-5. Then and there plaintiff No. 1 jumped over the land in presence of Md Montaz Ali, Md Garib Ullah and Md Rahim Ullah and expressed his right of preemption of the suit land and requested defendant No. 21 to transfer the same in favour of the plaintiffs on receipt of the consideration of the kabala, but defendant No. 21 refused the claim of the plaintiff's side. Thereafter, the plaintiffs collected the certified copy of the deed on 27-5-1998 AD and came to know that defendant No. 1, a stranger, purchased the suit property by a registered deed dated 3-5-90 AD at a consideration of Taka 3,50,000 only beyond their knowledge. The suit land was essential for the plaintiffs and the total area of the land owned by them would not exceed 60 bighas if the preemption was allowed. The plaintiffs were ready to pay the consideration money to defendant No. 1, So, the plaintiffs prayed for preemption of the land transferred by the kabala in question. 

 2. The suit was contested by defendants Nos. 1 and 21 by filing a written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable in its present form and was bad for defect of party. The suit property originally belonged to Md Afjal, the predecessor of both the plaintiffs and the defendants. Afjal died leaving behind 5 sons, named, Asrab, Turab, Majid, Kashim and Basid. Asrab died leaving behind 3 sons, named, Wajid, Wahid and Wasir. Wazid died leaving behind his son Samuj Miah, defendant No. 22 and daughters Maya Bibi and Sona Bibi, Wahid died issueless, Wasir died leaving behind his sons Moyna Miah and Lal Miah. Moyna Mia died leaving behind his wife Mahmuda, sons Saad Mia and Syed Miah and daughter Hasna Begum. Saad Miah died leaving behind his wife Laila Begum and daughter Sabina Begum. By an informal partition amongst the brothers Turab got plot No. 432 which is being possessed by defendants Nos. 1 and 21. The heirs of Kashim got plot No. 433, the heirs of Asraf got the dwelling house of plot No. 434, the heirs of Majid Ullah got plot No. 436 while the heir of Hashim got the land of Plots No. 436 and 437. Defendants Nos. 1 and 21 are co-sharers by inheritance in the khatian. The plaintiffs were offered to buy the suit property but they denied to purchase. The plaintiffs had purchased the land of plot No. 437. Defendant No. 1 after getting possession of the suit property on 3-5-1998 expanded his dwelling house therein by spending an amount of Taka 25,000 and also filled in a portion of the same through earthwork by spending an amount of Taka 30,000, planted some saplings of valuable tree by spending an amount of Taka 10,000. The plaintiffs had no possession in any portion of the suit property and they filed the suit with an intention just to harass the defendants. Plaintiff No. 1 never claimed the suit property from the defendants on 23-5-1998 as claimed by them. The suit property being adjacent to the dwelling house of the defendants they needed the same. So, the suit was liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 3. At the trial the plaintiffs examined 4(four) witnesses and on behalf of the contesting defendants also 4 witnesses were examined. The trial Court by its judgment and decree dated 18-5-2003 decreed the suit on the finding, inter alia, that the suit was filed within time and was not bad for defect of party. The plaintiffs were co-sharers in the khatian from which the land was transferred whereas the defendant was a stranger in the Khatian. The trial Court further found that the plaintiffs observed the formalities as required by Mohammedan Law to pray for preemption, namely, talab-e-mowasibat, talab-e-Ishaad and talab-e-tamlik. The trial Court further found that the defendant spent a sum of Taka 4,000 for the development of the suit land after purchase and directed the plaintiffs to pay the said amount to defendant No. 1-purchaser. 

 "My name is Hajee Md Monk Mia. I am the plaintiff No. 1. I am deposing for the plaintiffs' side. The suit property is a part of our predecessors' dwelling house, pond Barundi, etc. Abdul Rojak Dhan Mia, Abdul Hekim, Haji Abdul Bari, Ramjan Bibi, Abdul Gani, Alkas Bibi were the owners of the entire suit dwelling house and their names were recorded in 6 SA Khatians Nos. 9, 46, 98, 160, 200 and 267. I have submitted the khatians. The plaintiffs and the defendants Nos. 2-20 have been possessing the suit property jointly and living jointly. The proforma defendants Nos. 9-11 are our sisters. The defdt No. 21 was encircling the suit property by bamboo fencing in Jaistha and then I asked him the reason and he informed me that his brother Sefiqur Rahman has purchased the same. Both the purchaser and the sellers were in London at the time of transfer. Then and there I told the defendant No. 21 in presence of Montaz Ali, Garib Ullah and others to give me the land on receiving the money and I need the land. The defendant denied it saying that he was not the owner. I asked the defendant No. 21 as to date of purchase and consideration money, but he denied to disclose any thing. Then I went to the Biswanath SR office and came to know that a deed was registered in the name of the defendant No. 1 and collected the CC of the deed. I have submitted the CC of the deed. Goyesur Rahman, the attorney of the defendants Nos. 2-5, had sold out the land to the defendant No. 1. The consideration money of the suit land was shown as Taka 3,50,000 only but, in fact, the same was more than the actual market value. The sold land is unspecific. We need the suit land. The transfer was made beyond our knowledge and the deed was executed and registered beyond our knowledge. We need the suit property very much. The defendants Nos. 1 and 2 reside in separate dwelling houses and the defendant No. 1 is a stranger to the suit land. We were not served any notice before transfer. If the suit property is given to us through preemption then the area of our total land will not exceed 60 bighas. So, we have filed the suit for preemption under Mohammedan Law. We are ready to deposit the consideration money as per direction of the Court. The peripheral description of the suit in the deed is not correct. I have submitted the CC of the suit deed dated 3-5-98 AD being No. 1912 (Exhibit-1). I have submitted the original SA Khatian No. 98, 200 of 267 (Exhibits 2, 2A, 28). I pray for decreeing the suit. I have got a local investigation (sic) held a report was submitted by the Id Commissioner." 

 12. Besides the above, the learned Advocate for the plaintiffs had the option to apply to the Court for recording the deposition of PW 1 in Bengali as provided in the various Rules of Order XVIII of the Code, particularly rules 9 and 10. Not only that, before PW 1 put his signature in the deposition sheet his learned Advocate had the option to read the evidence recorded by the Judge and if there was any omission on the part of the learned Judge in recording the statements made before him by the PW in respect of the observance of the legal formalities condition precedent for filing a suit for preemption he could point out the same to the presiding Judge by filing an application invoking the provisions of rules 5 and 7 of Order XVIII of the Code. The plaintiffs had also the option to recall PW 1 involing rule 17 of Order XVIII of the Code read with section 138 of the Evidence Act, but nothing was done. Further, had PW 1 deposed as to the observance of talab-e-mowasibat and talab-e-Ishaad the same must have been recorded by the trial Court as from the style of recording of the deposition by it we have not found any dearth of language. PW 2, one of the two persons whose names were mentioned at the time of demanding talab-e-Ishaad also did not say anything about the reference of talab-e-mowasibat. In view of the above, we do not find any other alternative but to confirm the finding of the appellate Court that the plaintiffs failed to observe the legal formalities of talab-e-mowasibat and talab-e-Ishaad being the condition precedent to pray for preemption under the Mohammedan Law. But we do not agree with the finding of the appellate Court that defendant No. 1 was a co-sharer in the khatian as the Khatian from which the land has been transferred by the kabala in question does not show that either defendant No. 1 or his predecessor was a co-sharer therein. We find the finding of the trial Court that defendant No. 1 was a stranger in the concerned Khatian based on proper consideration of the evidence on record.
